extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents) before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) and USPTO disciplinary staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards governing interim suspension of a practitioner from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. §11.25, including what constitutes a 'serious crime', notice/response requirements, evidence, limited recognition to wind up matters, referrals for formal discipline, publication, and consequences for Customer Numbers/PKI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner notification of conviction (37 C.F.R. §11.25(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon being convicted of a crime in a court of the United States or any State, a practitioner subject to the disciplinary jurisdiction of the Office shall notify the OED Director in writing of the conviction within thirty days from the date of such conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory reporting duty; failure to timely notify can affect later disciplinary actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'serious crime' (37 C.F.R. §11.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Serious crime' includes any criminal offense classified as a felony under the laws of the United States, any state or any foreign country where the crime occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A felony conviction under state law therefore qualifies as a serious crime for purposes of interim suspension under §11.25.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'conviction' for disciplinary purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of 'conviction' includes any 'verdict or judgment finding a person guilty of a crime' and 'any entered plea, including nolo contendre or Alford plea, to a crime.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pled nolo contendere (no contest) or Alford pleas count as convictions triggering disciplinary processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED Director preliminary determination and filing of complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: After notification or receipt of certified court records, the OED Director shall make a preliminary determination whether the crime constitutes a serious crime warranting interim suspension and, if so, file with the USPTO Director a complaint against the practitioner predicated upon the conviction of a serious crime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The OED Director initiates the §11.25 process by evaluating seriousness and filing the formal Complaint when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence required to initiate USPTO Director action
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the court record, docket entry or judgment demonstrating that the practitioner has been convicted must accompany the complaint and be supplied to the USPTO Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Documentary proof of conviction (certified court record/docket/judgment) is necessary to trigger the notice and order procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of USPTO Director's notice and 40-day response requirement (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receipt of the certified court record and complaint, the USPTO Director shall issue a notice containing: (i) a copy of the court record, docket entry, or judgment of conviction; (ii) a copy of the complaint; and (iii) an order directing the practitioner to file a response within forty days establishing specified defenses or genuine issues of material fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner has 40 days from the notice to respond and must address the listed matters to avoid default interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permissible defenses in the practitioner's response
rubrics_metrics.description: The practitioner's response must establish a genuine issue of material fact that: (1) the crime did not constitute a serious crime; (2) the practitioner is not the individual found guilty of the crime; or (3) the conviction was so lacking in notice or opportunity to be heard as to constitute a deprivation of due process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only these specific factual showings will prevent the Director from deciding the request on the documentary record and entering interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing on documentary record unless genuine issue shown (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request for interim suspension shall be heard by the USPTO Director on the documentary record unless the Director determines that the practitioner's response establishes a genuine issue of material fact as to one of the enumerated defenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no genuine issue of material fact is shown, the Director will decide on the documentary record and may enter an appropriate final order despite any pending criminal appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: If genuine issue exists: dismissal of request and referral for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: If the USPTO Director is unable to make the documentary-record determination because there is a genuine issue of material fact, the Director shall enter a final order dismissing the request for interim suspension and enter a further order referring the complaint to a hearing officer for a hearing and entry of an initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Showing a genuine issue triggers the full hearing process rather than immediate interim suspension on the documentary record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim suspension warranted on felony conviction absent evidence of resentencing
rubrics_metrics.description: A felony conviction for a crime listed as a serious crime is sufficient to impose interim suspension under §11.25; a pending or attempted resentencing (e.g., under state law initiatives) does not prevent suspension unless the practitioner provides documentary proof that the felony has been mitigated to a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent bears the burden to provide results/resolution of any resentencing petition; failure to supply requested supplemental information supports interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition to practice for limited purpose (37 C.F.R. §11.58(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner subject to interim suspension may be granted limited recognition to practice before the Office for a short period (here, 30 days) solely for the purpose of facilitating compliance with the provisions of 37 C.F.R. §11.58(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited recognition is narrowly circumscribed to allow the practitioner to wind up or transfer client matters as required by §11.58.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 after suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. §11.58 (duties upon suspension or discipline), including requirements to notify clients, wind up matters, transfer files, and otherwise comply with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compliance with §11.58 is mandatory and the limited recognition period is intended to facilitate that compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of complaint for formal disciplinary proceeding (37 C.F.R. §11.25(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: If interim suspension is entered, the Complaint shall be referred to a hearing officer (here, at the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development) for the purpose of conducting a formal disciplinary proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspension does not end the process — a formal adjudication follows via referral to a hearing officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer filing and service requirements under 37 C.F.R. §11.36
rubrics_metrics.description: Within thirty days from the date of the Final Order, the practitioner's written answer to the Complaint must be filed with the hearing officer at the specified addresses; a PDF version must be filed via email; and a copy must be served on the OED Director by mail to the USPTO Office of the Solicitor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The order specifies both mailing and hand-delivery addresses and requires electronic PDF filing in addition to service on OED; strict compliance with filing/service instructions is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of interim suspension notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette stating the practitioner's name, registration number, and that the practitioner has been suspended on an interim basis for being convicted of the specified crime; disciplinary decisions are made publicly available (e.g., OED FOIA Reading Room).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication is part of the disciplinary record and public notice of interim suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to government entities and state bar authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice of the Final Order to appropriate employees of the USPTO, interested departments, agencies, and courts of the United States, and appropriate authorities of any state in which Respondent is known to be a member of the bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim suspension is communicated broadly to other governmental and licensure authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of Customer Numbers and revocation of PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate the practitioner's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers; the practitioner shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number nor have his name added to a Customer Number unless and until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Access and electronic authentication tied to Customer Numbers and PKI are disabled for the suspended practitioner until reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review of suspension does not stay the suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent seeks a review of the suspension, any review shall not operate to postpone or otherwise hold in abeyance the suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative review does not act as an automatic stay; practical effect is the suspension remains in place during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by certified mail to addresses provided; good cause to proceed if addresses previously used
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of certified mail to addresses provided by the respondent and addresses the respondent previously used to correspond with the Office supports a finding of good cause to proceed with a Final Order even if the mailed items were not delivered or picked up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may proceed with the disciplinary process where it has utilized respondent-provided or previously used addresses despite nondelivery, establishing sufficient service attempts.
